name: GetVocal AI agents
operator: GetVocal AI (the vendor); each customer is the operator of its own use
basis: GetVocal AI's own public product, blog, customer-story, privacy and status pages, and its published llms.txt
what: GetVocal AI's voice, chat, WhatsApp and email agents for enterprise contact centres, built in its Agent Builder and supervised by people through its control console.
note: A scan of a product as its vendor documents it, not of any one deployment. Made by the report studio: a researcher-assessor, a challenger, then the scorer. I56 is shown for the AI-disclosure fact; the Openness 1 level stands on I20 and I58.
grant_note: Not measured. No deployment shape for this product is published in the capability grammar.

findings.finding: Argued. What the source says: the large-spanish-telecom customer story, about an unnamed operator, says each interaction began with clear disclosure that the caller was speaking with a virtual assistant. This is a vendor statement about one customer's deployment, not about what the product does. The EU AI Act blog says Article 50 disclosure applies from 2 August 2026, advises a disclosure node as the first step of every Context Graph, and says to implement disclosure nodes. So an opt-in disclosure node is a documented product pattern, which supports mode available and the configuration disclosure-node. No page I read says disclosure is the default, and the Glovo story (listed in not_credited) points the other way, so default would be wrong. Grade documented is right: it is a statement, not an observed call. Weaknesses: the deployment is unnamed and cannot be checked, and the blog gives advice to deployers, not a described setting. Key point: O1 does not depend on I56. The Openness 1 rule is I20 plus any of I56, I22, I58, and I58 (data it uses is described, enterprise-ai-agents FAQ) satisfies it alone. Removing I56 leaves the card at O1. Suggest the scan note says that I56 is shown for the AI-disclosure fact and that the O1 level stands on I20 and I58. The card is not overstated, but a reader could think I56 carries the level.

The three spans are in the live pages but not in the HTML text the page shows when stripped. They sit in the collapsed FAQ answers of the voice and control-tower pages, held in the page's FAQ JSON-LD and Sanity data in the raw HTML. I checked the raw: voice FAQ (CRM question) says 'the agent can update a booking or a customer record exactly as your policies allow'; voice FAQ (hallucination question) says 'it escalates to a human operator instead of improvising'; control-tower FAQ ('Is GetVocal's platform agentic?') says 'it cannot take actions the graph does not contain'. All three spans are exact and under fifteen words, so they pass. The capture hashes the raw page, so a reader can verify, but the scan notes could say the text is in an FAQ answer so a reviewer who reads the visible page is not misled. For I08 the sentence is a capability statement about a CRM integration, documented and default is acceptable; the Nicomatic story (Sam logs the event in the ISO database, notifies the supervisor) is a concrete second source for I08 and would make A3 and A4 less dependent on one FAQ sentence.

The indicator is 'There is a way to pause or stop it'. The control-tower page says 'Operators take over instantly to protect the customer relationship' (a human taking over one conversation) and llms.txt says to override any agent. Neither describes pausing or stopping an agent. The EU AI Act blog describes system-level and use-case-level pause only as what 'a robust kill switch implementation' should include, as advice, not as a GetVocal feature. The scan note itself says no page describes pausing or stopping an agent. Crediting I39 on a take-over is a nearby fact, not this one. It does not change a level here (Control 3 also needs I41 and I43, and I41 is an operation fact graded documented), but the answer should be removed or the note should state that take-over is the only evidence and the indicator is arguably not shown.

Both indicators have needs: operation and are graded documented, so they do not count towards any level (the card output confirms Control stays at C1 and Reach and Autonomy do not use them). That is correct as scored. The sources do say it: the escalation blog says 'GetVocal generates an immutable audit trail for every AI action' (span found, ten words) and the Control Tower FAQ says the agent cannot take actions the graph does not contain. These are vendor descriptions, so keeping them in the scan as documented is acceptable if the gate permits it; they must stay uncounted. The I41 scope asks that the log cover what the agent does; the span says every AI action, which fits, but the blog also says audit trails for every AI decision, with node-level timestamps.

Credit to Nicomatic is right in kind: the story names the customer and the span 'Sam automatically logs the event in the ISO database' is in the page (the page also says Sam notifies the supervisor and escalates when required, and that Sam is deployed across sites in France, the UAE, India, Senegal and Morocco). It names a customer for the capability that acts, which meets S1; it gives no usage figures and does not give seats or installs. Problem: the note cites an 'Equans France news item (over half of calls resolved without human intervention in 90 days)'. That item is not among the scan's captured sources and I could not find it on any of the nine getvocal.ai pages or the status page (Equans appears only as a logo image on the enterprise page). A claim in a note with no captured source breaks the rule that every answer has a public source. Remove the Equans sentence or add and capture its source. Also note the telecom story gives figures (42% of eligible calls resolved through self-service, 99% routing accuracy) for the conversational agent that could be an alternative S1 anchor, though the operator is unnamed.

The scan carries no S4 answer, which I think is right. I looked in llms.txt, the enterprise page, the control tower page and the blog pages for an MCP server, an agent card or an API documented for agents to call, and found none. The REST API in the escalation blog is GetVocal sending a handoff payload to a customer's agent desktop (an interface it consumes and pushes to), so it does not meet the S4 scope. Reach 2 is right and the next unlock is correctly I13 and S2.

Card A4 R2 C1 O1. A4 rests on I08 (a CRM FAQ sentence), I10 or I12 or I13 (I10, from llms.txt) and I18 (a Control Tower feature page, marked available). All three are vendor prose: artefacts in the sense that they are statements on public pages, but no operation evidence (observed or measured) supports any of them, and A4 depends on a feature available only when operators configure human validation. The card marks this availability, which is correct. The I10 span ('Agents handle voice and chat across your existing stack') does not itself name several systems; the systems (CRM, CCaaS, telephony, helpdesk) follow in the next sentence of llms.txt, so the span is exact but the note relies on the text after it. Consider using the named Genesys Cloud and Salesforce integrations from the escalation blog (already behind I11) or the enterprise FAQ ('take action across your systems') as the I10 span. A4 is argued as sufficient but thin: the wording 'Orchestrates' (multi-step workflows across systems) is supported only by capability statements, with Nicomatic's Sam (log, notify, escalate) the one concrete example. R2 rests on I10 and I11 (named integrations), fine. C1 rests on I38 (llms.txt plus the escalation blog on Operator View, configured per node), fine and marked available. O1 as above.

Checked against the fetched sources: spans found and exact (apostrophe differences ignored), all under fifteen words (longest I58, 14 words), credited to indicators whose text they show. I03 llms.txt describes Agent Builder as no engineering. I11 escalation blog names Genesys Cloud CX API v2 and Salesforce Service Cloud REST API. I17 and I18 Control Tower page ('Guide the Edge Cases', 'Validate for Sensitive Actions'); mode available is right because the blog says operators configure which nodes need validation. I20 llms.txt. I21 EU AI Act blog says each node defines data access, logic, outputs and escalation conditions, graded documented, tier declared is fine. I36 llms.txt names GDPR and the EU AI Act as 'aligned', which is a self-description, not a legal determination; documented is acceptable. I38 mode available: the page does not say it is on by default. I54 status page shows a 28 September 2026 incident, call gateway, with Investigating, Identified and Resolved updates with times (investigating span is from 2:46 PM UTC); public status page, grade documented fine. I58 enterprise FAQ. I67 and I68 are marketing statements, graded documented and tier declared, no level used. S3 llms.txt resolves (observed, fetched 2026-11-10, capture hash recorded).

The studio's reply is true as far as it goes: the scan note now says I56 is shown for the AI-disclosure fact and that Openness 1 stands on I20 and I58, and the card computed here confirms O1 uses I20, I56 and I58 with I58 alone sufficient. But the I56 note still names the Glovo deployment ('many restaurant partners never realised they were speaking with AI') and not_credited cites https://www.getvocal.ai/customers/glovo as its source. That page is not among the nine captured sources of the scan (captures list has no Glovo URL), and the sentence appears in none of the nine fetched pages. I fetched the live Glovo page myself: it says 'Many restaurant partners never realized they were speaking with AI' (so the claim is true), but a note and a not_credited entry resting on an uncaptured page break the rule that every answer has a public, captured source. Add the Glovo page to the sources and capture it, or drop the Glovo sentence from the I56 note and the not_credited entry. The same applies to the configuration note 'seen in one deployment' which is fine. Round one's Equans problem recurred in a smaller form.

Answered. The three spans do not appear in the visible stripped text, but I confirmed each exactly in the raw HTML: voice FAQ JSON-LD ('...so the agent can update a booking or a customer record exactly as your policies allow'; '...it escalates to a human operator instead of improvising'), and the control-tower raw ('...but it cannot take actions the graph does not contain'). Spans are under fifteen words. The notes now say 'An FAQ answer on the ...' and name the question, which fixes the reader's problem. Grades documented and mode default are fair. Answered. I39 is gone from answers and is listed in not_credited with a reason that matches the pages (take-over of one conversation and override are not pause or stop; kill switch appears only as advice). The note does not name any page not in the scan: the not_credited source is the captured control-tower page. Control 3 stays out of reach, correctly; card output shows C1 with next I23.

Answered. Both remain documented, needs operation, so they are not counted (card output: Control uses only I38). I41 span ('GetVocal generates an immutable audit trail for every AI action' region) still found in the escalation blog raw text, and the I41 note's list (graph node, data sources accessed, timestamp) matches the blog sentence. I48 note now states it is an FAQ answer and the span is exact in the control-tower raw.

Answered. The Equans sentence is removed. The note now says Nicomatic's Sam 'logs confirmed production events in the ISO database, notifies the supervisor and escalates when required'; the Nicomatic page says 'Sam automatically logs the event in the ISO database, applies the correct data-handling rules, notifies the supervisor and escalates when required', so it is supported. Weak point worth knowing: the page names the customer and the deployment (sites in France, UAE, India, Senegal, Morocco) but gives no usage figures, so S1 rests on 'names a customer for the capability that acts', which the scope permits.

Answered by agreement, no S4 answer. I looked for an MCP server, agent card or agent-facing API in the fetched pages and llms.txt and found none; the REST API in the escalation blog is a handoff payload GetVocal sends to a customer's agent desktop.

Changed since round one, re-checked. Span 'Agents handle voice and chat across your existing stack (CRM, CCaaS, telephony, helpdesk)' is exact in llms.txt, 13 words, indicator I10 (several domains or systems) fits, grade documented, mode default. The weakness: this is a single marketing sentence on llms.txt. Any one of I10, I12, I13 satisfies the A4 and R2 rules, and I10 is the only one answered for Autonomy; R2 has I11 as a second, more specific source (named Genesys Cloud and Salesforce integrations in the escalation blog). The studio answered the round-one finding; nothing wrong remains.

findings.answer: scan note and not_credited wording check
findings.finding: Changed notes check (D). I08, I40, I48, I10, S1 notes name only pages in the scan. The I56 note's mention 'the EU AI Act blog advises deployers to add a disclosure node' is supported ('Implement Article 50 disclosure nodes', 'Disclosure node as first step in every Context Graph'). The I56 span ('clear disclosure that the caller was speaking with a virtual assistant', 11 words) is exact in the telecom page ('Each interaction began with clear disclosure that the caller was speaking with a virtual assistant'). The only uncaptured reference is Glovo (see I56 finding).

Arguing against A4, R2, C1, O1. A4 = I08 plus I17 or I18 (A3), plus I10, plus I18. It rests on three vendor-prose statements: one FAQ sentence in JSON-LD (I08, 'the agent can update a booking or a customer record'), the llms.txt stack sentence (I10), and the Control Tower 'Validate for Sensitive Actions' feature (I18, mode available, only when operators configure validation nodes). These are dated page statements, not adjectives, but none is observed or measured; the only concrete deployment (Nicomatic's Sam logs events, notifies the supervisor) supports I08 in practice and is not cited under I08. Without I18, A falls to A3 (I17 also satisfies A3 but A4 needs I18 or I19); without I08 the A3 and A4 rules fail and the dimension drops sharply. So A4 hangs on I08 and I18 together, and the card correctly marks A as available. 'Orchestrates' is a strong label for 'works across several systems' given only capability statements. R2 rests on I10 and I11, either sufficient; I11 is a specific, documented fact (REST API, Genesys Cloud CX API v2, Salesforce Service Cloud REST API), so R2 survives removal of I10. C1 (a stated level one) rests only on I38, from llms.txt plus a blog saying operators configure validation nodes; it is mode available, shown as such, and removing I38 would give no Control level (I47 is not answered). O1 stands on I20 plus I58 without I56. I20 is a vendor description of purpose in llms.txt and the FAQ; adequate. Modes are shown honestly (A4, C1 marked available; O1 and R2 default). Remaining suggestion only: consider citing the Nicomatic page as a second source for I08.

Re-verified against live fetched sources: spans exact and under fifteen words (longest I58, 14), right indicators, grades and modes consistent. I54: status page shows Sep 28, 2026 incident with timed updates (4:11 PM and 5:04 PM UTC on the page); note supported. I36: llms.txt names GDPR and EU AI Act as alignment, a self-description, documented is acceptable. I03 fits the scope of a no-engineering builder. S3: llms.txt resolves, observed, hash recorded.

responses.response: No change to I56: mode available with the disclosure-node configuration and grade documented stand. O1 holds without I56 (I20 plus I58); we propose the scan note add one sentence: 'I56 is shown for the AI-disclosure fact; the Openness 1 level stands on I20 and I58.'

No change in grade or count: both stay documented and uncounted as operation facts; I48's note now says the text is an FAQ answer.
Removed the Equans sentence from the note so it rests only on the captured Nicomatic story; the In production badge is unchanged.
Agreed, no S4 answer; nothing changed.
I10's span now carries the named systems (CRM, CCaaS, telephony, helpdesk), verified literally in llms.txt at 13 words. A4 R2 C1 O1 is unchanged and A4 stays marked available.
Passed; no change beyond the I10 span and the I40 FAQ wording noted above.

I03.n: Agent Builder is described as a no-engineering builder that makes agents from the customer's SOPs, transcripts and policies.
I03.span: Build, debug and tune production-ready, multilingual agents from your SOPs

I08.n: An FAQ answer on the voice page (the CRM question) says agents write to connected systems through scoped integrations, such as updating a booking or a customer record.
I08.span: the agent can update a booking or a customer record

I10.n: The llms.txt says the agents work across the customer's CRM, CCaaS, telephony and helpdesk systems.
I10.span: Agents handle voice and chat across your existing stack (CRM, CCaaS, telephony, helpdesk)

I11.n: The handoff payload is described as sent over a REST API to the agent desktop, naming Genesys Cloud and Salesforce integrations.
I11.span: delivered via bidirectional REST API to the unified agent desktop

I17.n: The Control Tower page says the agent consults a human expert on edge cases.
I17.span: AI consults a human expert when encountering edge-case scenarios.

I18.n: The Control Tower page says the agent asks a human to approve critical decisions before executing them.
I18.span: AI proactively asks a human to approve critical decisions before executing them.

I20.n: The llms.txt says the agents resolve customer conversations end to end inside the customer's business rules, with human approval on high-stakes actions; the Control Tower FAQ says the agent cannot take actions its graph does not contain.
I20.span: Agents resolve customer conversations end to end while staying inside your business rules

I21.n: Each node of an agent's graph is described as defining the data it may access, its outputs and its escalation conditions.
I21.span: Each node defines what data the AI can access

I36.n: The llms.txt names GDPR and the EU AI Act as the frameworks the platform is aligned with.
I36.span: GDPR and EU AI Act aligned

I38.n: llms.txt says high-stakes actions such as large transactions, high-value returns and sensitive data get human-in-the-loop approval. A GetVocal blog on escalation says operators configure, in the Control Tower's Operator View, which decision nodes require validation.
I38.span: with human-in-the-loop approval on high-stakes actions

I40.n: An FAQ answer on the voice page (the hallucination question) says requests outside the agent's authority are escalated to a human operator.
I40.span: it escalates to a human operator instead of improvising

I41.n: The vendor describes an audit trail for each agent action, recording the graph node, data sources accessed and timestamp.
I41.span: GetVocal generates an immutable audit trail for every AI action

I48.n: An FAQ answer on the Control Tower page says agent actions are limited to those present in the business-rule graph.
I48.span: it cannot take actions the graph does not contain

I54.n: The public status page publishes incident reports with timed updates, including a call platform outage on 28 September 2026.
I54.span: We are currently investigating an issue affecting our call platform.

I56.n: In one deployment for an unnamed large Spanish telecom operator, each call opened with a disclosure that the caller was speaking with a virtual assistant. No GetVocal page states that agents disclose they are AI by default or documents a disclosure setting; the EU AI Act blog advises deployers to add a disclosure node. In the Glovo deployment, GetVocal reports that many restaurant partners never realised they were speaking with AI.
I56.span: clear disclosure that the caller was speaking with a virtual assistant

I58.n: The agents are described as grounded in the customer's call scripts, help documents, CRM records and past transcripts.
I58.span: a living model of your call scripts, help docs, CRM records and past transcripts

I67.n: The Control Tower dashboard is described as tracking KPIs, escalation trends and CX quality.
I67.span: Track KPIs, escalation trends, and CX quality across all journeys.

I68.n: Corrections, escalations and validations are described as fed back to refine the agents continuously.
I68.span: Every correction, escalation and validation feeds back as a learning signal.

S1.n: GetVocal's Nicomatic story names the customer and says its assistant Sam logs confirmed production events in the ISO database, notifies the supervisor and escalates when required.
S1.span: Sam automatically logs the event in the ISO database

S3.n: An llms.txt resolves at the site root (fetched 2026-11-10).
S3.span: GetVocal builds AI voice and chat agents for regulated, high-volume customer operations.

not_credited.what: GetVocal's Glovo story says many restaurant partners never realised they were speaking with AI.
not_credited.why: Shown because it bears on disclosure; the card counts disclosure only where a deployment is configured for it.

not_credited.what: There is a way to pause or stop the agent (I39).
not_credited.why: The pages describe operators taking over one conversation and supervisors overriding an agent; pausing appears only as advice on what a kill switch should include, not as a described GetVocal feature.
